title: 14th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 56 members present. Most of it was ministerial question time: Minister of Construction and Infrastructure Dr Abdulla Muttalib answered questions from about 30 members on stalled water, sewerage, harbour, road and reclamation projects, saying many Fenaka contracts were terminated and handed to MWSC or MTCC and that the budget does not cover all signed projects. The Speaker also referred the President's nominee for the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives to the Human Rights and Gender Committee, and the Manadhoo member opened the preliminary debate on the government's bill amending the Criminal Procedure Act; two members spoke before the sitting closed at 11:02 to give time to committees, with no vote taken.

items.title: Praises and prayers; opening of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 56 present, 3 on leave, 4 on official travel

items.title: Question to the Minister of Construction and Infrastructure from the Kendhoo member on the stalled Kendhoo water and sewerage project, with follow-up questions on projects in many islands
items.outcome: minister answered; many members asked follow-ups

items.title: Question to the Minister of Construction and Infrastructure from the Kendhoo member on problems upgrading Dhonfanu harbour
Presidential nomination of a member for the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives (Law 6/2006, Article 5)
items.outcome: referred to the Human Rights and Gender Committee

items.title: Preliminary debate on the government bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act (Law 12/2016), sponsored by Manadhoo member Husnee Mubarik
items.outcome: sponsor presented; two members spoke; debate not concluded, sitting adjourned

speakers.name: Dr. Abdulla Muttalib
positions: As Minister of Construction and Infrastructure, said stalled water and sewerage projects, where Fenaka-led contracts were terminated, are being handed to MWSC and tender boards.
Said the budget does not cover all signed projects, so projects are being prioritised with the Finance Ministry, and he could not give island-by-island dates without details.
Said harbour issues such as Dhonfanu involve design-and-build contractor liability and that the new harbour projects depend on available finance.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked when the halted Kendhoo water and sewerage works would be finished, noting reports that only small portions remained.
Asked when Dhonfanu harbour problems would be solved, and urged the issue be addressed even within a new project.
Raised a point of order that the Machchangolhi North member was allowed to finish a question while the Vilimale member was not.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked how far the Hithadhoo water works and the halted Hithadhoo harbour project had progressed.
Raised a point of order on how long the minister stays to answer, which the Speaker did not accept as one.
Said Hithadhoo harbour works have stalled three times in six months over excavator and crane diesel supply, and asked how work will proceed.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked how long the government needs to finish the Kurinbi water and sewerage project, which he said is running slower than before.
Asked what is known about the Kurinbi harbour work now being done by MTCC.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked about the Kunahandhoo water and sewerage work, which he said stands at 0 percent, leaving the island without services.
Asked whether the government has a target date for completing water and sewerage everywhere and whether any island will be left behind.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked for restart and completion dates for halted water and sewerage works in Fulhadhoo and Fehendhoo.
Said stored materials there are deteriorating, and asked for dates when work will start, finish and services be delivered.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked when the halted Landhoo water and sewerage project, where money was spent on unskilled labour, would restart after tender award.
Presented the government's bill to amend the Criminal Procedure Act, covering cybercrime investigation powers, data preservation and bail rules.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ali
positions: Asked when water and sewerage can be set up on the reclaimed land at Dhuvaafaru, which has long been completed.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Said the Ihavandhoo reclaimed land is not filled to the needed level, and asked for a fix and a ministry visit.
Asked when halted water and sewerage works in Molhadhoo and Maarindhoo would restart.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Raised Innamaadhoo's water and sewerage work started under the previous government and the Inguraidhoo harbour allocation in the 2024 budget.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked what the minister knows about the halted Maamendhoo water and sewerage works, saying residents, including a woman, suffered serious injury.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Asked roughly how many projects were signed around the 2023 presidential election without financing being raised, and how much finance they need.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked for the latest update on the Addu bridge project, which opposition parties say has been halted.

speakers.name: Ahmed Riyaz
positions: Asked when the slow Thimarafushi road project, now left by the Indian subcontractor of RDC, would resume, and about the Veymandoo and Kinbidhoo causeways.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked about plans for the remaining Maradhoo roads, whether by tar or paving, after earlier roads were done through FCOMS.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked about the Holhi water and sewerage project, the start of Foddhoo harbour, and the restart of the halted Velidhoo harbour.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rasheed
positions: Asked about halted harbour projects in Omadhoo, Dhigurah and Mandhoo, and when work to stop Dhangethi's erosion would start.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked when water and sewerage systems in Narudhoo and Feevaku would be finished.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Asked when asphalting of the Isdhoo-Kalaidhoo main road would start, and when the Kalaidhoo-Dhanbidhoo causeway and Maabaidhoo shore protection would be sped up.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shifaz
positions: Asked how soon Markarath harbour, under work for about 15 years, can be finished, and what is being done now.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abdul Rahman
positions: Asked when work to provide water and sewerage on Hinnavaru's reclaimed land would start at the latest.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Asked what the government will do to hold accountable those responsible for the delayed, contract-based project, and whether any MDP member benefits from it.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked whether budgeted but unstarted projects will begin this year, and whether the ministry has emergency funds for erosion.
Said the Kanditheemu council's letter has gone unanswered.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Raised Vilimale residents' hardship from the road to the bridge being damaged and flooded, before the Speaker asked him to stop.

speakers.name: Mohamed Siruhaan
positions: Asked when work on Hithaadhoo harbour would start and when Dharavandhoo roads would be asphalted.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Asked for an update on the Greater Malé bridge (Thilamale link) project and on reclamation projects from the previous government.

speakers.name: Hassan Waheed
positions: Asked when work on Buruni harbour and the Madifushi roads would restart, and when the Vilufushi airport would begin.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked when the long-halted Fuvahmulah road works would restart.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked when shoreline protection would begin at Kelaa beach, whether the Kelaa channel would be dredged, and about Filladhoo's beach.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Backed the bill, saying it helps investigate cybercrime and set clear bail rules, citing a case of money drained from bank accounts; urged committee work with experts.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Backed the bill as important for cybercrime investigation and for clear bail rules, saying judges and experts have asked for it to be refined.

decisions: President's nomination to the Human Rights Commission of the Maldives referred to the Human Rights and Gender Committee under Rule 123(n).
Sitting recessed from 10:27 to 11:00, then adjourned at 11:02 to give committees time; the Criminal Procedure Act amendment debate was not concluded.
Next sitting set for Tuesday 16 July 2024 at 9:00.
